_doc: Measured carriageway widths (2026-11 survey on the NLSC 2024 orthophoto, WMTS PHOTO2 z20, about 0.14 m/px; cross-sections rotated along each road with a metre ruler, kerb to kerb including 機慢車道 and kerbside parking, excluding sidewalks, 騎樓, medians and ditches; the biggest changes re-measured blind by a second surveyor). tools/build_map.py apply_roads() sets each OSM way's w (and lanes where given) after the block fill and the grade separations; 'was' is the width OSM / the class default gave, checked on every build. Only widths that differ by 0.8 m or more are listed. 'measured' entries come from cuts on that road; class entries (source says 同類道路) use the typical width of a measured sample of the same kind of lane. 'marks' lists the painted markings of a way read off the same orthophoto: centre (double-yellow 雙黃實線, yellow 單黃實線, yellow-dash 黃虛線, white-dash 白虛線, none, median 分隔島, pair / pair-other: one of the two one-way ways OSM splits a two-way street without a median into; pair paints the 雙黃線 along its edge facing the other way, pair-other nothing there, and neither gets a white edge line on that side), edge (white edge lines) and lanes (lanes per direction); optional walk gives the sidewalk as surveyed: {n, s} or {e, w} widths in metres for the side facing that way (0 = none) and col, its paving colour; js/map.js draws these instead of the class defaults (primary..tertiary get lines, others none). 'features' are painted spots in game metres: box 網狀黃線 (centre x, z, len along the street; kerb to kerb unless w), zebra 斑馬線 (centre, ang = direction of the street it crosses in degrees, w across it, len of the stripes), stop 停止線 (centre, ang, w across), bikebox 機車停等區 (centre, ang, len deep, w wide); zebras the game already lays at an OSM crossing / signal junction carry osm: true and only break the lines there. Optional cv in a marks entry puts the centre line cv metres off the middle of the carriageway (+ = (-uz, ux) of the way's direction), where one side is wider (kerbside parking). 'shift' moves OSM ways sideways onto the carriageway the orthophoto shows: at = anchors [x, z, v], v the offset in metres along (-uz, ux) of the way's direction (+ = the top of an _survey/xsec.py cut) of the middle between the kerbs from the OSM line; tools/build_map.py shift_roads() interpolates between anchors, holds 40 m past the end ones and eases out over 40 m more, and moves shared nodes in every way; the old line stays in r.osm (trees, lamps and shop fronts are laid out on it, then the spots the moved road covers move past its new kerb).
